claims.text: HfZrTiTa0.53 has a reported yield strength of 786 MPa.
HfZrTiTa0.53 has a reported compressive strength of 1314 MPa.
HfZrTiTa0.53 has approximately 13.5% terminal strain under compression.
The tensile ductility and load-bearing reliability of HfZrTiTa0.53 are limited.
Adding approximately 2 at.% Nb and annealing at 600°C for 2 hours will refine the microstructure of HfZrTiTa0.53.
The Nb addition and annealing treatment will reduce the grain size.
Nb will segregate to grain boundaries during annealing.
Nb segregation and annealing will form ductile intergranular films or phases at grain boundaries.
Annealing will produce precipitates that contribute to the proposed grain-boundary structure.
The proposed ductile intergranular phases will delay crack initiation.
The proposed grain-boundary structure will encourage more uniform plastic deformation during tension.
The intervention will promote grain-boundary sliding and healing mechanisms during tensile deformation.
Dislocation-based strengthening will be retained in the matrix after Nb addition and annealing.
At room temperature and a quasi-static strain rate below 10^-3 s^-1, the modified alloy will achieve at least 20% tensile uniform elongation.
The modified alloy will retain yield strength within ±10% of 786 MPa.
The modified alloy will preserve compressive properties comparable to those of baseline HfZrTiTa0.53.
The modified alloy will preserve impact-triggered energy release in thin-steel-target penetration tests.
WFeNiMo fragments provide a relevant benchmark for fragment energy release in thin-steel-target tests.

contradictions.description: The reported 13.5% value is alternately described as compression uniform elongation, terminal strain, and the baseline for tensile uniform elongation. Terminal compressive strain and tensile uniform elongation are different measurements and cannot be used interchangeably.
Reaching 20% from a 13.5% baseline is approximately a 48% relative increase, not the stated approximately 15% relative improvement.

The prediction requires yield strength to remain within ±10% of 786 MPa, whereas the falsification rule addresses only a decrease greater than 10% and does not test the upper side of that stated interval.
